title: Vanishing in the universal curve test
statement:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

be a base-change square where
$X\to S$ is an affine smooth morphism of relative dimension one (in
the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]) and $X$ is affine, $S$ is
the spectrum of a
normal domain $A$ with
algebraically closed fraction
field $L$, and $K/L$ is an extension of algebraically closed fields.
The map $g$ is the composite $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induced by the given inclusions $A\subset L\subset K$. Let $d$ be an integer invertible on $S$. The coefficient $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ is the constant abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and higher direct images are those of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Then

$$
R^qh_*(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)=0\qquad(q\geq1).
$$

proof.text: Identify A’s affine function field with L using the fraction-ring algebra equivalence. Transport the algebraically closed structure and compose the resulting map with L → K. The chosen Cartesian square is converted to the source CurveTestDatum orientation by the pullback universal property.

Replace the signed coefficient d by d.natAbs. IsUnit d implies d ≠ 0 and hence d.natAbs ≠ 0; the cast of d.natAbs is a unit because d is either nonnegative or nonpositive. For each q ≥ 1, write q as a natural number and apply the cyclic local-vanishing theorem.

In degree one use CurveTestDatum.exists_cover_cohomologyMap_eq_zero, which packages slicing, normal-base reduction, algebraically closed invariance, torsor trivialization and spreading. In degrees at least two, base change preserves smooth relative dimension one and the resulting affine smooth curve has subsingleton constant-sheaf cohomology.
